Train with us from first licensure to doctoral leadership. Then, feel supported as you launch your career as an alumnus with the benefits of Launchpad. 

ADMISSIONS & AID
FLEXIBLE HYBRID LEARNING

Attend classes online from the comfort of your own home and with the ability to learn from the best professors around the country. Come to campus for meaningful handson learning and clinical training.

Learn More About Becoming a Student
ACAHM ACCREDITED

The Accreditation Commission for Acupuncture and Herbal Medicine accredits acupuncture and herbal medicine programs across the country. Most states require that you have attended an ACAHM accredited school.

Accreditation & Approvals
CAB APPROVED

California is unique. They have their own programmatic requirements and its own licensing exam, the CALE. By attending AIMC, you are prepared to practice in integrative settings across the country!

Explore Choosing a School
STELLAR BOARD SCORES

Over the last several years, AIMC has continued to perform in the top five for CALE performance. For most other states of the nation, NCBAHM licensing exams are necessary. AIMC outperforms the national average year over year!

Berkeley, where our Journey Began!
Shining bright for over 30 years!

AIMC has been honored to serve the community and train the next generation of acupuncturists for over 30 years. It never would have been possible without all of the love, support, and integrity of our students and community. We look forward to the new chapters lying ahead as the field changes and we evolve along with it. Time is such a gift, and it's been an honor to spend it with you.

Explore Berkeley

Keeping it Weird Together in Austin!

In spring of 2024, AIMC went from AIMC, Berkeley to AIMC as a whole: Acupuncture and Integrative Medicine College, a graduate school with two locations, Berkeley and Austin. Having two locations, each with its own distinct group of staff and campus culture, creates dual venues for innovation and fresh approaches. These locations support and enhance each other, demonstrating that we truly are better together.

Understanding Winter Pain: Insights from Traditional Chinese Medicine

Biologically, What's Happening? The idea that cold weather exacerbates joint pain is supported by various physiological mechanisms. Cold temperatures may not directly cause arthritis or structural damage to joints, but they do influence pain perception in the body. One primary factor is the viscosity of synovial fluid, which thickens in colder conditions. Thank You for Your Support!

We owe our presence and success to the incredible generosity and unwavering support of our donors, sponsors, and community partners. While some of our private donors prefer to remain anonymous, we hold deep gratitude and appreciation for each and every individual who has contributed to our mission at AIMC. Our community partners foster an enriched environment that will yield practitioners who are able to support diverse patient populations.

Your support enables us to continue spreading integrative health and wellness with compassion and dedication.

Thank you to our Partners

We are deeply grateful for the generosity and ongoing support of our donors, sponsors, and community partners. While some contributors choose to remain anonymous, each and every donation plays a vital role in advancing our mission at AIMC.
